_comment: Copilot CLI >= v1.0.72 fires agentStop when the main agent finishes a turn, so boy-scout-check scans after the work instead of before the next prompt. agentStop's documented output power is block/force-continuation only, not additionalContext injection; the hook therefore queues advisory findings for userPromptSubmitted, whose additionalContext is injected into the model-facing prompt by Copilot CLI >= v1.0.65. boy-scout-check deliberately never emits decision: "block": the Boy Scout nudge is advisory. VS Code agent mode documents this event as Stop (PascalCase), and its agent-hooks are Preview and off by default; this timing fix remains unverified there pending a local canary. route-prompt remains first under userPromptSubmitted and provides routing/plan-gate/security salience where additionalContext is consumed. Older Copilot versions ignore unsupported events or JSON output as a harmless no-op. route-prompt/session-start self-detect the surface: Claude Code events carry hook_event_name and get plain stdout; everything else gets the JSON shape. preToolUse is consumed as JSON permissionDecision deny, which is how guard.* enforces hard-blocks on Copilot. See docs/enforcement-surfaces.md for the guaranteed-vs-instructed matrix. The per-tool 'matcher' field is intentionally omitted (Copilot supports it, but): VS Code agent mode emits write tool names that cannot be fully enumerated (camelCase str_replace/insert/etc.), so guard.* must see every tool call and self-filter on file-path+content -- a 'matcher' regex like 'edit|create' would blind it to those VS Code writes and open a security gap. The fast self-exit on non-write calls is the deliberate cost of that coverage; do not add a matcher here.
